title: Release audit: Quoted secret labels are not fully redacted. For a message such as `'token': 'ab
summary: Handle a closing quote after a quoted label before looking for the separator, or parse quoted keys and values; add tests for quoted labels and JSON snippets and assert the value is absent from captured output.
requirements: When a message contains a secret label enclosed in matching single quotation marks, followed by a separator and a value, the displayed text keeps the label and both of its quotation marks as they are, keeps the separator as it is, and replaces the value with the masking placeholder.

When a message contains a secret label enclosed in matching double quotation marks, including the JSON-style form where the label's closing quote is directly followed by a colon, the displayed text keeps the label and both of its quotation marks and the separator as they are, and replaces the value with the masking placeholder.
When the value of a quoted secret label is itself quoted, the value's own quotation marks stay visible around the masking placeholder and no character of the value remains.
When the value of a quoted secret label is unquoted, the whole value up to the next whitespace or the end of the message is replaced by the masking placeholder.
No character of a secret bound to a quoted label appears in any text the session displays, including reply text, engine state and engine error text.
Masking a message that is already masked changes nothing further.
Each masked value carries exactly one masking placeholder, and repeated separator characters between a quoted label and its value stay visible.
A message with no secret bound to a label, and a message that only mentions a secret label without binding a value to it, is displayed unchanged.
The quotation marks that a fix introduces as part of the label never cause a neighbouring word, a separator or trailing punctuation to be masked.

The automated test suite covers a single-quoted secret label with a single-quoted value, a double-quoted secret label with a double-quoted value, and the JSON-style form where the label's closing quote is directly followed by the separator.
The existing test suite continues to pass without any test being weakened, skipped or deleted.
acceptance: A session line carrying a single-quoted secret label with a single-quoted value displays the label and its quotes, the separator, and the masking placeholder in place of the value; searching the displayed line for the value finds nothing.

A session line carrying a double-quoted secret label with a double-quoted value, in the form where the label's closing quote is directly followed by a colon, displays the label and its quotes, the colon, and the masking placeholder in place of the value; searching the displayed line for the value finds nothing.
A single-quoted secret label followed by an unquoted value displays the value replaced by a single masking placeholder, with nothing of the value left and no neighbouring word masked.
Masking an already masked message that carries a quoted secret label leaves it unchanged, and each masked value carries exactly one masking placeholder.
Messages without a secret binding, and messages that only mention a secret label, are displayed unchanged.
The automated test suite contains passing checks for the single-quoted form, the double-quoted form and the JSON-style form, and the whole suite passes.
plan_goal: Forgel Code: interactive agent client instead of a command wrapper

checks.criterion: A single-quoted secret label with a single-quoted value is masked in full when displayed.
A double-quoted secret label with a double-quoted value in the JSON-style form is masked in full when displayed.
An unquoted value after a quoted secret label is masked with exactly one placeholder and no neighbouring word masked.
Masking is idempotent and each masked value carries exactly one placeholder.
Secret-free text and label-only mentions are displayed unchanged.
The suite covers the single-quoted, double-quoted and JSON-style forms and the whole suite passes.

result.summary: Extended the session masking so a secret label wrapped in matching quotation marks is recognised as a label rather than as the opening quote of its value. `forgel_code/interactive.py` gains `_label_quote_end`, which decides that a quote after a label closes the label when no value character touches it (a separator, whitespace, punctuation or end of message follows), and `_quoted_binding`, which takes the value bound to that quoted label through `=`/`:` separators or as an adjacent quoted run; `_binding` now consults both before falling back to the previous behaviour. Quoted labels therefore keep the label, both of its quotes, the separator and any repeated separators visible, while the value is replaced by the single `[redacted]` placeholder — inside the value's own quotes when the value is quoted, up to the next whitespace when it is not. `tests/test_redact.py` adds coverage for the single-quoted label with a single-quoted value, the double-quoted label with a double-quoted value, the JSON-style form (`{"token":"abc123"}`), an unquoted value after a quoted label, repeated separators, non-masking of neighbouring words and trailing punctuation, idempotence and exactly-one-placeholder for the quoted forms, absence of any value character, and a session-level reply carrying a quoted label. Full suite: `python -m pytest -q` -> 297 passed, 262 subtests passed.
assumptions: A quoted value belongs to the quoted label as a whole: the marker sits inside the value's own quotes, so the rest of the quoted run is masked too, matching the existing behaviour for unquoted labels with quoted values (`password: "hunter2 and more"`).
A quoted label binds a value only through an `=`/`:` separator or an immediately adjacent quoted run; a plain word after the closing quote still counts as a mention and stays visible.

checks.criterion: A single-quoted secret label with a single-quoted value is masked in full when displayed.
The suite covers the single-quoted, double-quoted and JSON-style forms and the whole suite passes.

review.summary: The change fixes the quoted-label masking gap in the shared redaction step (`_binding` in `forgel_code/interactive.py`) instead of at a display site: `_label_quote_end` decides whether the quote after a label closes the label (separator, space or trailing punctuation) or opens a value (alnum/value characters glued to it), and `_quoted_binding` then resolves the value either through a separator (reusing `_separator_end`/`_bound_value`, so repeated separators stay visible and unquoted values stop at whitespace) or as an adjacent quoted run. Label, its two quotes and the separator stay outside the masked span, and the value's own quotes stay around the placeholder through the existing quoted-span logic, so single-quoted, double-quoted and JSON-style (`"token":"...`) forms all mask fully while `the word "token" appears here`, `say 'password' please`, `"secret" is missing` and `the 'token' was rotated.` stay unchanged. Tests were added, not weakened: `tests/test_redact.py` gains cases for the single-quoted, double-quoted and JSON-style forms, unquoted values after quoted labels, repeated separators, neighbour non-masking, idempotence with exactly one placeholder, absence of any value character, and an end-to-end session check with a quoted label in an engine reply; the existing reply stub was extended (not relaxed) and the pre-existing assertions on `token: [redacted]` still hold. QA reported pass for the local and environment acceptance checks and no test removals. The commit is scoped to the two needed files with no unrelated, temporary or generated content.

requirements.requirement: FR-1: A single-quoted secret label keeps the label and both quotes and the separator, and the value becomes the masking placeholder.
requirements.note: `_label_quote_end` treats the closing quote as part of the label when a separator follows; tests `'token': 'abc123'`, `'password'='hunter2'`, `'secret': 'swordfish'` check the exact displayed text.

requirements.requirement: FR-2: A double-quoted label, including the JSON-style form with the closing quote directly followed by a colon, keeps label, quotes and separator, and masks the value.
requirements.note: `"token": "abc123"`, `"password" = "hunter2 and more"`, `"secret" : "swordfish"` and `{"token":"abc123"}` are covered with exact expected output.

requirements.requirement: FR-3: A quoted value keeps its own quotes around the placeholder with no character of the value left.
requirements.note: The mask reuses the existing quoted-span logic; `test_no_character_of_a_quoted_secret_stays_visible` asserts the value is absent while the quotes remain.

requirements.requirement: FR-4: An unquoted value after a quoted label is masked up to the next whitespace or end of message.
requirements.note: `_quoted_binding` delegates to `_bound_value`, and `'token': abc123 now` -> `'token': [redacted] now` is tested.

requirements.requirement: FR-5: No character of a quoted-label secret appears in reply text, engine state or engine error text.
requirements.note: The fix sits in the shared `redact` path used at every display point; the session-level test asserts `abc123` is absent from the engine reply output.

requirements.requirement: FR-6: Masking an already masked message changes nothing further.
requirements.note: Quoted forms were added to the idempotence table in `test_redaction_is_idempotent`.

requirements.requirement: FR-7: Exactly one placeholder per masked value, and repeated separators between a quoted label and its value stay visible.
requirements.note: `'token':: abc123` -> `'token':: [redacted]` and `"token" == "abc123"` are tested; placeholder counting is asserted (`count("[redacted]") == 1`).

requirements.requirement: FR-8: Messages with no secret binding, and messages that only mention a secret label, are displayed unchanged.
requirements.note: `_quoted_binding` returns no span without a separator or adjacent quoted run; `test_a_quoted_label_does_not_mask_its_neighbours` covers four mention-only sentences.

requirements.requirement: FR-9: The label's quotation marks never cause a neighbouring word, separator or trailing punctuation to be masked.
requirements.note: Returning the mask span after the label's closing quote keeps the surrounding text intact; `say 'password' please`, `"secret" is missing` and `the 'token' was rotated.` are asserted unchanged.

requirements.requirement: FR-10: The automated suite covers single-quoted label with single-quoted value, double-quoted label with double-quoted value, and the JSON-style form.
requirements.note: Three dedicated test methods cover exactly these forms, plus the JSON-style case where the label's closing quote is directly followed by the colon.

requirements.requirement: FR-11: The existing suite continues to pass with no test weakened, skipped or deleted.
requirements.note: No test removals were detected and no assertions were relaxed; the reply stub was extended with a quoted label while keeping the previously asserted `token: abc123` fragment, and QA reported the full suite and acceptance checks passing.

requirements.requirement: AC-1: Single-quoted label with single-quoted value masks the value and the value cannot be found in the displayed line.
requirements.note: Exact-output and substring-absence assertions plus QA's acceptance check.

requirements.requirement: AC-2: Double-quoted label with double-quoted value (closing quote directly followed by a colon) masks the value and the value cannot be found.
requirements.note: Covered by the JSON-style and double-quoted tests with exact output and absence checks.

requirements.requirement: AC-3: Single-quoted label with unquoted value yields a single placeholder, nothing of the value left, no neighbouring word masked.
requirements.note: `'token': abc123 now` -> `'token': [redacted] now` with placeholder count 1 and absence assertions.

requirements.requirement: AC-4: Masking an already masked quoted-label message leaves it unchanged, one placeholder per value.
requirements.note: `test_redaction_is_idempotent` includes the quoted forms and asserts `redact(once) == once` with `count("[redacted]") == 1`.

requirements.requirement: AC-5: Messages without a secret binding and mention-only messages are displayed unchanged.
requirements.note: Covered by the neighbour non-masking test and the existing mention/secret-free tests, which remain unchanged.

requirements.requirement: AC-6: The suite contains passing checks for the single-quoted, double-quoted and JSON-style forms and the whole suite passes.
requirements.note: The three test methods exist; QA's environment and acceptance runs reported pass with exit 0.
